free_tier.stated: 3 GB TOTAL PER GAME, not per file. The 3 GB number is corroborated three ways this session: the official 9-year-old changelog post ('Max filesize for builds has now been bumped to 3GB instead of 2GB. Go upload big things!'), a developer post 4 months old ('the upload limit for total game size on GameJolt has been extended to 3GB'), and a departing developer 11 months old ('GAMEJOLT'S LIMITATION ON THE GAME FILE SIZE OF MAX.3GB'). Earlier it was 1 GB, then 2 GB per build ('that's per build, meaning that if you have multiple builds for different platforms, each one is allowed to be up to 2GB').

egress.terms: Free, Cloudflare-fronted (Server: cloudflare, cf-cache-status: HIT on the storefront). No billing. No separate CDN hostname was resolvable from here (mproxy./build./games.gamejolt.net all NXDOMAIN), so downloads are served through the main site edge.

tooling: Web dashboard only ('Add Your Game' at /dashboard/games/add) - no upload API, no SFTP, no CLI. Read side is ordinary HTTPS GET from game pages. The public Game Jolt API v1_2 is for auth/scores/trophies/data-store, not file transfer.
chaining: unlimited games per account x 3 GB each. That is the only multiplication available, and it is account-bound rather than file-bound - 500 GB would need ~167 games, and 3 GB is below the brief's 500 GB-per-unit filter unless you count per-account aggregate.

extras.agent_focus: The code-forge seam: OSS project hosts, software-download directories, game/mod distribution and mirror services. Question for each: (a) any published byte quota, (b) is upload possible over SFTP/rsync/SCP/SSH rather than a web form, (c) is there a public download CDN, (d) does it need an approved project or can any account create one, (e) per-file cap. Round 2 flagged that SourceForge has no published quota and serves over plain SFTP with a global mirror CDN, and that an rclone-backend enumerator would score the niche as empty. This slot tests that class systematically. Every number below was read live or from a dated archive capture this session.

binding_note: the per-object cap sets the shard size and therefore the object count; it bounds the total more tightly than any headline quota
